reason: The specified JROM Test transcript was mostly mic-test fragments and the FIX-B4 synthetic transcript had only three short lines, so this hand-written 60-second multi-speaker transcript is used for meaningful summary/action-item scoring.

lines.name: Maria
lines.text: Thanks everyone. The purpose of this meeting is to decide how we will roll out the transcript cleanup feature for the meet prototype.

lines.name: Leo
lines.text: From engineering, the provider abstraction is ready. Claude, Codex, and Ollama can all be called through the same service, but we still need a default Ollama model.

lines.name: Nina
lines.text: For product, accuracy matters more than speed. If the model misses action items or invents decisions, the cleanup button will not be useful to customers.

lines.name: Omar
lines.text: I tested the local machine this morning. It can run the larger models, but anything over about one minute per transcript will feel too slow for a first version.

lines.name: Maria
lines.text: Decision: we will benchmark five Ollama candidates today and choose the top three by accuracy first, then speed as the tiebreaker.

lines.name: Leo
lines.text: I will run the benchmark script, save every model output, and write the ranking document with timing and scoring notes.

lines.name: Nina
lines.text: I will review the top three outputs tomorrow and pick the default model for the transcript cleanup workflow.

lines.name: Omar
lines.text: I will monitor CPU and memory during the first customer demo so we know whether we need a smaller fallback model.

lines.name: Maria
lines.text: Great. We are not adding UI in this batch. The only deliverable is the benchmark report and the installed models for the next cleanup feature.
